items.title: Drugs: list tirzepatide and Wegovy, mazdutide per case
items.text: Strongest Chinese and head-to-head data, and Wegovy alone has outcome data

items.title: Who prescribes: the weight clinic, endocrinology, nutrition
items.text: Only trained, authorized doctors, with a pharmacist reviewing every prescription first

items.title: Rules: check the label threshold, weight loss is self-pay
items.text: Track efficacy, safety and adherence, with the first review six months after launch

notes: Three proposals, which the last page asks the committee to vote on one by one. First, the drugs: list tirzepatide and semaglutide 2.4 mg, sold as Wegovy. Tirzepatide produced the largest weight loss in the only head-to-head trial and in its Chinese trial, and its price fell by about 80% this year. Wegovy is the only drug with cardiovascular outcome evidence and gained a cardiovascular indication in China in December 2025. Mazdutide, a domestic drug, has good Chinese data but no outcome data, and at retail prices costs about ¥2,020 per 4 weeks, more than the other two, so we propose buying it case by case rather than listing it. The rest stay off the formulary. Second, who prescribes: the weight management clinic, endocrinology and clinical nutrition, by doctors who have been trained and authorized, with a pharmacist reviewing each prescription before it is dispensed. Third, the rules: check each patient against the label threshold for that drug, bill all weight-loss prescriptions as self-pay, track three groups of measures, and review the program six months after launch.
